image_prompt.text: A wide floor of sprung trampoline beds set edge to edge in padded frames, with angled wall trampolines around the sides, so the bounce is the point of the space
An open floor beside the beds sized for a crowd of visitors to gather, queue and rest between bounces
A tall distinct structure over the park — signage or a big central attraction — visible from anywhere on the floor so visitors can orient themselves
The park entrance, placed so arrivals look straight out across the trampoline floor

layout_placement.text: Arrival point at the park entrance, players enter here

notes: no genre: 'a big trampoline park' names a place, not a game type. no-genre.md's rule against inventing a genre is what kept this off obby-platformer despite the jumping being the activity.
all five axes left at default, so the route is P0. Indoor warehouse vs outdoor park is genuinely open and is the first open question; either answer stays on P0.

physics-rig taken from Simulation via options.md for the trampoline beds. The no-genre table and the universal six both miss, and this was the nearest row, but its own wording (ramps, ragdoll props, breakable assemblies) is not what the prompt described. Text rewritten to the prompt's subject.
preset Social Space kept whole, landmark-focal included, though the prompt implies nothing about a landmark.
scale assumed block on the strength of 'big'; the trampoline beds themselves are room-band detail, so this may be one band too coarse.

open_questions.ask: Is this an indoor trampoline park inside a warehouse-style building, or an outdoor one in the open air?
Besides the main trampoline floor, which attractions should the park have — a foam pit, a dodgeball court, a ninja/obstacle course, or slam-dunk lanes?
What's the smallest thing you want to be able to make out — individual trampoline beds and padding, whole courts and the building around them, or the park plus its car park and surrounding streets?
How should it look — bright stylized toon colours, or a realistic modern-urban leisure centre?

captured: a trampoline park as the entire scene
trampoline beds as the defining geometry
'big' as a size cue, taken as the block band

skill_gap.name: no bounce surface option
skill_gap.why: The trampoline beds are the whole scene and no row in the no-genre table, the universal six, or options.md describes a sprung bounce surface. physics-rig ('ramps, ragdoll props, and breakable assemblies') was the nearest fit and had to be rewritten wholesale, so a real missing option is hidden behind a stretched ID rather than surfacing as an unmatched request.

notes_for_us: no-genre.md says to ask only about an axis 'that would change the route', but SKILL.md step 5 says to ask when a named thing could be built more than one way and the ways differ in what gets built. Indoor vs outdoor is the biggest build decision in this prompt and costs no route, so the two rules disagree. I followed step 5 and asked.
Nothing in options.md covers a bounce surface, trampoline bed, or foam pit. physics-rig is the only near miss and its wording points at ragdoll comedy props, not a sprung floor.

All three no-genre presets (Explorable Place, Social Space, Open Sandbox) are passive places to look at or wander. An activity venue — trampoline park, water park, arcade — has no preset, so accepting the closest one adds crowd and landmark options the prompt never implied.

The scale rule says to ask only when the prompt 'names an extent without naming what lives in it'. 'A big trampoline park' names both and still does not settle the band, and the rule gives no guidance for a bare adjective like 'big'. I asked anyway.
This pilot's prompts.json has no 'enriched' field, so coverage.enriched_invented could not be filled the way LANE-BRIEF describes.
